title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: MCP-based agents for US Government clouds
summary: The roadmap facts and the published blocking path and API are accurate. Hold the briefing because it treats authenticated MCP actions and agent-blocking applicability as undocumented despite documentation covering their respective classes; it also overstates the data an agent can reach.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes support for developers to build Microsoft 365 Copilot agents using MCP servers.
claims.quote: We’re introducing support for Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot . This update enables developers to build Copilot agents using MCP servers

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically describe this MCP government-cloud roadmap rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP agents GCC GCC High DoD licensing license government custom actions; "564607" MCP government default rollout licensing. Opened overview-plugins, build-mcp-plugins, known-issues, prerequisites and the Copilot service description.

claims.claim: An MCP plugin is a custom action within a declarative agent.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or REST APIs that have an OpenAPI description.

claims.claim: The MCP plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server; it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.claim: The plugin manifest does not package or host the running MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server; it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.claim: For declarative-agent MCP plugins, Copilot resolves tools dynamically from the server at runtime by default.
claims.quote: For plugins based on an MCP server, Copilot resolves the plugin's tools dynamically at runtime by default, directly from the MCP server.

claims.claim: A developer can instead pin a fixed tool set in the plugin manifest.
claims.quote: When building the agent, a developer can optionally pin a fixed set of tools in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.claim: The Copilot service description lists declarative agents as not currently available in DoD.
claims.quote: | Declarative agents | Yes | Yes | Yes^8^ | Not currently available |
claims.fix: Retain the attribution to the service description, and add: 'The declarative-agent overview instead lists limited DoD support for pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/overview-declarative-agent#national-cloud-support.

claims.claim: The service description limits GCC High declarative-agent support to Agent Builder agents and agents published through admin controls.
claims.quote: GCC-High currently only supports declarative agents created using Agent Builder and those published via admin controls.
claims.fix: Retain the attribution, and add: 'The declarative-agent overview also states that GCCH supports pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit, as well as Agent Builder.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/overview-declarative-agent#national-cloud-support.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default state of this government-cloud MCP enablement on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP-based agents government clouds default state rollout GCC High DoD enablement; "564607" MCP government default rollout licensing. Read the roadmap, known-issues, build-mcp-plugins, prerequisites and service description; no rollout default.

claims.quote: Searched: "MCP" "government" "boundary" Copilot plugins; Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP plugins government cloud data boundary authenticated custom actions. Read overview-plugins and data-privacy-security, plus gov-overview excerpts; none specifies this rollout's external-server boundary.

claims.quote: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data aren't currently available in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The OAuth walkthrough obtains an access token on behalf of the signed-in user for each MCP call.
claims.quote: Copilot then uses the registration to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user each time the agent calls the MCP server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: It is not stated whether authenticated MCP calls fall under the Government restriction on authenticated custom actions.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or REST APIs that have an OpenAPI description.
claims.fix: Replace the uncertainty statement with: 'Learn classifies MCP plugins as custom actions, so its Government restriction on authenticated custom actions covers authenticated MCP actions. The roadmap nevertheless lists MCP-based enablement as launched; it does not explain that conflict.' Keep the known-issues and overview-plugins citations. Remove or replace the corresponding open question with 'How is the roadmap launch reconciled with Learn's restriction on authenticated custom actions?'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MCP and API plugins can create, update and delete data through natural-language prompts when the connected service supports those operations.
claims.quote: users can ask a declarative agent to query an MCP server or REST API for information and, when supported, create, update, and delete data and objects through natural language prompts.

claims.claim: Dynamic discovery allows the server's tool set to change without repackaging or republishing the agent.
claims.quote: Dynamic tool discovery means you get the latest tools the MCP server exposes without waiting for the agent to be repackaged and republished.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: "MCP" "Government" "license" "agents" Copilot Chat. Read prerequisites, build-mcp-plugins, the Copilot service description and copilot-license-options; these give general agent rules but no licensing rule specific to this rollout.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page includes Microsoft 365 Copilot Business among its agent access licensing models.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business - A standalone SKU introduced for small and medium businesses. Provides Copilot agent access aligned with Microsoft 365 Business plans.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page includes Microsoft 365 E7 among its agent access licensing models.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E7 (Frontier Suite) - A bundle that includes Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Agent 365 capabilities for enterprise customers.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page describes usage-based agent access without a full licence, with configuration limitations.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (pay-as-you-go) - Tenants can enable agent access without a full license, with some limitations to agent configuration options.

claims.claim: The general usage-based agent billing model measures consumption in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Consumption is measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Agents published by the organisation go through admin approval before being made available to its members.
claims.quote: Before you make these agents available to members of your organization, these agents go through an admin approval to ensure compliance and readiness.

claims.claim: The agent inventory is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents.
claims.quote:
1. Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
2. Select Agents > All agents.
3. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.

claims.claim: The block path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote:
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.
In the Block agent or Unblock agent pane that opens, select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: The block API is a preview Microsoft Graph beta operation.
claims.quote: | Block (preview) | POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block` | Block a package to prevent its usage. |

claims.claim: The documented agent-blocking control restricts use across the organisation using the same controls as other apps.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that general agent blocking applies to a declarative agent using an MCP plugin.
claims.quote: You can manage agents for Copilot by using the Microsoft 365 admin center. You can enable, disable, assign, block, or remove agents for your organization, and manage Copilot capabilities.
claims.fix: Remove the statements that blocking applicability to an MCP-based declarative agent is unconfirmed. Replace them with: 'The control blocks the selected agent. Blocking an agent does not necessarily block a shared MCP server or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions. Retain the separate national-cloud and API limitations; do not imply that blocking the agent blocks every connected component.

claims.claim: The cited user-interface documentation gives no explicit DoD-specific availability statement for blocking.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365 MCP servers declarative agents block government GCCH DoD. Read agent-actions and manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps; cloud notes address GCCH/GCCM publishing, not DoD blocking.
